definition: AbstractConcreteDisjoint abstract concrete means ∀ x, abstract x → ¬ concrete x, for independently supplied classification predicates. It does not define either classification or assert that every candidate belongs to one of them.
note: Required classification policy for the intended P2-B/P3 wrapper, alongside its exercise-to-thin-power dictionary and owner power-to-concrete constraint. The generic predicate alone remains a proposition, not a theorem about arbitrary labels. It imposes neither exhaustiveness nor a ban on incoming abstract causation, and does not classify passive recipients as abstract. See docs/notes/causal-power-concreteness.md. #1103: the same proposition is the required disjoint field of the shared Classification (DEF-CONCRETE-ABSTRACT-CLASSIFICATION); for the adopted esse sense it is derived, not stipulated (DEF-ABSTRACT-NO-ESSE-IN-RE).
